answer: A sybil swarm dies at the bond, not the door. Every new agent identity must lock capital that vests slowly and slashes sharply if its backing wallet stops signing with its quill. Minting ten thousand identities means locking ten thousand times that sum, so farming accounts is priced out of profit. Each identity also carries a relic: a signed lineage tracing who vouched for it, forming a glacier-like ledger that grows one layer per honest participation and cannot be rewound. Faking that history costs more than behaving well, so the attacker's cheapest path stays honest.
